correctness.rationale: A direct derivation of the state bijection uses upper and lower rim words x,y: the rung has both values x_(i−1) XOR x_i and y_(i−1) XOR y_i, so x_i XOR y_i is constant b. Properness is exactly the word constraints and x_i≠b; b≠0 forces b=3 and even alternating x. At b=0, for omitted colour c, a rim edge is in the switched colour pair iff x_i≠c and a rung is in the pair iff exactly one of its two bounding rim letters is c. The pair subgraph is consequently exactly the cycles formed by runs and their bounding rungs, or the isolated upper/lower rim cycles if c is absent. A run cycle avoids the fixed vertex iff it avoids both end positions; the lower rim switch in the absent-colour case produces b=3. At b=3 the two rim matchings of either colour 1 or 2 are complementary, so that colour with the rungs forms a single alternating Hamilton cycle through u_0. Only the 1,2 lower rim switch is allowed there. The triangle-free property follows from the cited general proposition; directly, two moves at one colouring with different colour pairs already force different swap pairs on the edges on which the two outcomes differ, and distinct moves with the same pair change disjoint components, not one component. Independently checked all ten witness moves by their changed intervals: the 0-based (left,right,omitted colour) triples are (2,3,2),(1,2,1),(3,3,2),(2,2,3),(1,1,1) and (4,4,2),(2,2,2),(3,3,3),(2,4,2),(3,3,1). Each is internally bounded by the omitted colour, so the prefix leaves each move valid. For n=3 the only word is 132; for n=4 the words are 1212,1232,1312, with the latter two adjacent only to 1212; the extra leaf gives the claw. The supplied scripts were inspected, not run.

evidence: The general triangle-free theorem applies directly. The proved parity-dependent hypercube-with-leaves theorem is for crossed prisms; the precursor class theorem gives one equivalence class for ordinary prisms.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Triangle exclusion solves the lower bound only, and the class theorem is a connectivity statement, not a classification of adjacency. The distinct crossed-prism theorem does not apply upon relabeling the ordinary prism family.

evidence: The normalized graph is the literature's KE_v for the ordinary prism. The cyclic word presentation is an equivalent reformulation of that edge graph by the rim/rung XOR relation, not the triangular-prism vertex Kempe graph in arXiv:1503.03430. The latter has two vertex-colouring classes.

originality.rationale: The 2017 article contains precisely the fixed-vertex formulation, the generic triangle exclusion, and a crossed-prism classification. Its remarks on ordinary prisms report small cases and the difficulty of exact form, not the claimed adjacency theorem. Ordinary-prism uniqueness of the edge-Kempe class is also known. Neither those results nor retrieved records about other cubic graphs give the full ordinary-prism word correspondence or the uniform five-cycle witnesses.
residual_risks: The specific attribution of the earlier degree sequence and exceptional leaf in the frozen prior-work paragraph is not pinned to a located passage; these data are not the distinctive contribution credited here.
An obscure equivalent normalized word model or even-rim construction could escape the bounded search; close same-day records do not in themselves establish any order of priority.

value.rationale: A full move-preserving model for an established reconfiguration graph answers a more useful question than its size or connectivity: it permits adjacency to be read directly from a cyclic word for every rim size. The explicit five-cycle families and uniform parity-dependent exceptional leaf give concrete global information beyond finite enumeration and distinguish the ordinary family from the known crossed-prism structure.
